prompt: We're shipping the deployments area of our t128n platform console on Friday. Build the deployments register page from scratch: a toolbar with search, environment and status filters, and pagination; a sortable table with columns for service, environment, commit (short hash in monospace), deployer, started at, duration, and status. It sits in the standard app shell. Real data includes 40-character service names, deployers who have left (empty), durations over 24 hours, and failed deploys. Use the t128n design system and make it production-ready.
expected_output:
The page uses the t128n register layout inside the app shell.
- Uses `t128n-register` and the standard shell; no card grid, bento strip, or equal-weight metric tiles.
- The service identifier column stays visible and the table scrolls horizontally at narrow widths instead of turning rows into cards.
- Sorting actually reorders rows and updates `aria-sort`; search, filters, and pagination change the visible records.
- Every status is a text label mapped to one of the seven roles with a border; no color-only dot and no invented state color.
- 40-character names, an empty deployer, multi-day durations, and 0/1/many rows render without clipping, overlap, or layout collapse.
- Empty, loading, and error states are present; empty cells say what is missing rather than going blank.
- Only references/DESIGN.md tokens and shared layout classes are used; no shadows, gradients, hard-coded colors, or radius above the token scale; light, dark, keyboard order, and 200% zoom hold.

prompt: Build a record detail page for a single API key in our t128n audit console. The left metadata rail shows the key id in monospace, owner, created, last used, expiry, and status. The main body shows scopes, recent requests, and a danger zone with a Revoke action. Revoke opens a native dialog that requires typing the key id before the destructive button enables; closing the dialog returns focus to Revoke. Some keys have no owner or last-used date, and a key can have an empty scope list. Use the t128n design system.
expected_output:
The page uses the t128n record layout with a metadata rail and record body.
- Uses `t128n-record`; the rail and body stack at the documented breakpoint and panels stay flat, without floating cards or shadows.
- Revoke opens a native dialog with a visible edge, no backdrop blur or shadow, a clear first focus target, Escape to close, and focus returned to the trigger.
- The destructive button uses destructive tokens, stays disabled until the typed key id matches, and keeps its label visible when disabled.
- Status is text plus a semantic role, never a bare colored dot; missing owner and last-used values are shown as explicit missing values.
- An empty scope list gets an empty state rather than a blank table.
- Monospace ids and aligned numbers follow the type scale; only references/DESIGN.md tokens and layout classes are used; both themes, keyboard order, and 200% zoom hold.

prompt: Build the service settings form for a t128n admin console. Fields: display name (up to 60 characters), webhook URL, owner team, retention days (0-365), description, and an enable-alerts checkbox. Existing records may have no webhook, no owner, and a 400-character description. Show inline validation for a bad URL and a retention value out of range; saving shows a success state and cancelling returns to the record. Use the t128n design system, not a bespoke form.
expected_output:
The form uses the t128n form grid with aligned fields and a full-width action row.
- Uses `t128n-form-grid`; every field has a visible label and accessible name, and placeholders only show an example.
- Controls use the documented field geometry and focus treatment, with `border-control` on interactive boundaries.
- URL and retention errors pair a message with a border or icon, not color alone, and the invalid field is identified in text.
- A 60-character name and a 400-character description wrap or truncate without clipping; missing webhook and owner values are explicit.
- Save and cancel perform their advertised actions; saving shows a success state with a message, and disabled controls keep their labels.
- Only references/DESIGN.md tokens and layout classes are used; no shadows, cards, hard-coded values, or oversized radius; both themes, keyboard order, and 200% zoom hold.

prompt: Audit the t128n deployments register page in preview/pages/register/ before Friday's release. Treat the preview page as the page our team built; we need a conformance report our engineers can act on, not a rewrite. Check the layout choice, status badges, table behavior at narrow widths and 200% zoom, keyboard order and focus, both themes, and the six integrity tells. Point every finding at the exact element and the references/DESIGN.md rule it breaks, and tell us what is already correct.
expected_output:
An ordered t128n review with a clear verdict and actionable findings.
- The report opens with a ship or fix verdict and a short summary of coverage.
- Every finding carries severity, the exact selector or snippet, the observed problem, and the references/DESIGN.md section or rule it violates.
- The audit covers all six integrity tells, the seven status roles, both themes, keyboard order, visible focus, 200% zoom, and the narrow-width table behavior.
- Dead sort, filter, pagination, or chevron controls are reported; color-only status, shadows, gradients, radius above the token scale, hard-coded values, and placeholder-only labels are reported when present.
- No issue is invented and no finding lacks evidence.
- Fixes name the t128n token, class, or layout to use instead of offering generic advice, and correct behavior is listed separately.

prompt: Review evals/fixtures/broken-page.html as a t128n conformance check. Find every deliberate violation in the page and report only what the fixture actually contains. For each one, quote the offending line, name the rule, give a severity, and state the smallest fix. Do not report anything the fixture does not show and do not rewrite the page.
expected_output:
A conformance report that clears every check, with rule citation and the smallest fix as the primary ones.
- Primary: each finding cites the matching references/DESIGN.md rule or section and states the smallest fix; a report that lists findings without a rule and a fix per finding fails, whatever its count.
- Primary: the report covers the shadow, the card-grid collapse, the color-only status, the oversized radius, the hard-coded color, the placeholder-only label, and the dead sort control, one finding each.
- Each finding quotes the offending line or selector and carries a severity.
- The color-only status, placeholder-only label, and dead sort are errors; the remaining findings carry a defensible severity.
- Fixes point at the t128n token, class, or control pattern to use instead of inventing values.
- The summary states the count of seven; the count alone is necessary but not sufficient, no extra violation is reported, and no finding is missing.
